summary: ```# 【Marvelous Designer】Learning Day - Hat Making Collection p05 Pure Enjoyment Edition 4_Painter's Hat ## Introduction In this tutorial, we will learn how to make a beret using Marvelous Designer. We will go through the steps of creating linked plates, adjusting the simulation, and refining the design to achieve the desired look for a painter's hat. ## Creating the Beret Base First, create a single plate using the previous sheep design and copy it to create six identical plates. Since we have copied six plates, we can select them directly and set them as linked plates. ### Sewing the Plates Next, use the line sewing tool to sew their sides together. For convenience, we can freeze the plate in front of us in the middle and turn on the other plates to simulate them automatically. After that, activate the plate to simulate them together. ### Printing the Plate To print the whole plate, press the W key and click on the plate to create a pin to fix it. Without the key, you can press the W key again to create a pin on the plate for fixing. ## Starting the Simulation Now, to start the simulation, select these plates and drag them up a little with the square wheel. Upon starting the simulation, you will see that the plate is fixed in the 3D window. ### Adjusting the Plates We need to make adjustments to these plates. Berets and suretees have a distinctive characteristic where the top of the hat expands outwards first before closing at the bottom. 1. On the left and right sides, add two straight points close to the bottom. 2. Pull them out a little bit using the edit board tool. After pulling them out, since they are all linked boards, opening the simulation will apply our modifications to the board. The plates should now resemble a common beret hat. Pull the bottom white down a little bit to make the thickness of the hat thicker. If you want the top to be looser, move the top point up slightly. ### Corner Adjustments Following these adjustments, you may notice sharp corners at the edges. To correct this, we will use the circular curve tool to round the corners on both sides. ## Preparing the Head Band The beret hat is unique compared to other hats as it should cover the head without slipping. Therefore, we will first create the headband and then fix it near the model for adjustments. 1. Draw a width approximately three times the model's head size. 2. Create a rectangular shape for the height. Press CTRL+D to create a symmetrical board and use the line powder tool to sew the two sides together. To ensure simulation stability, reduce the strength of the plate, the range, and the thickness of the collision. ### Positioning the Head Band Press SHIFT+F to position the board near the head of the virtual model. After opening the simulation, the board will sew together automatically, but it may not fix well near the virtual model. 1. If the board is narrow, pull it a little wider. 2. To adjust the width of the board, copy a piece of fabric and assign new fabric to the two newly created boards. ### Fixing the Board After rearranging the board and making it wider, we will fix the front end of the board for convenient adjustments. Use the function of fixing to the virtual model by clicking the board to the center, then the front position of the virtual model's forehead. While dragging the board in the simulation state, it should hang well near the model's forehead. ## Final Adjustments The eyebrows and eyelashes area might have a relatively small grid, making it easier to hook the board. Adjust as needed using the selection grid tool to pull out their grid separately. ### Physical Properties Adjustment Once the headband is nearly positioned correctly, we can adjust the physical properties of the board. Increase the fabric friction to prevent sliding, making it easier to fix in the desired position. 1. If the bending strength is too high, reduce it to allow better adherence to the head. 2. Adjust the position of the tie after reducing the bending strength. ### Color and Particle Adjustments To improve visibility, switch the color of the fabric to black. If the hairband and hair appear different, adjust the particle diameter of the hairband to ensure proper proximity to the head. Finally, merge the front and back panels, and adjust the fake sewing needle position. Choose a red color for the fake sewing needle and ensure it aligns correctly for a realistic look. ## Simulation and Refinement Once adjustments are complete, freeze the plate to prevent further movement. Use the positioning ball tool to select the plate of the hat and move them to the intended area. 1. Use the line sewing tool to sew the complete line at the bottom, filling from left to right. 2. Open the simulation, dissolve the hardening, and delete fixed needles as needed. ### Material Properties Change the main fabric of the hat to wool, reducing the particle diameter for detailed folds. Adjust the contact thickness to 1 for better results. To create a puffy beret effect, manually drag points to achieve the desired shape. If making a painter's hat, adjust accordingly for less puffiness. ## Conclusion Once all adjustments are made, you can apply elastic along the seam line for extra folds. Set the elastic ratio to 98 or 95 to enhance the realism. Finally, after manually adjusting the panels and ensuring all elements are cohesive, display the virtual model and turn on the simulation. Thank you for watching, and see you next time! ```
